techStack: React 19 with react-dom 19; no UI component library — plain HTML elements with custom CSS
TypeScript with strict-ish config: noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch enabled; strict is NOT set explicitly
moduleResolution: 'bundler' (Vite); allowImportingTsExtensions: true; verbatimModuleSyntax: true (type imports must use 'import type')
jsx: 'react-jsx' — no manual React import needed in JSX files; noEmit: true (TS only type-checks)
Build: Vite 6 with @vitejs/plugin-react (Babel-based); vite.config.ts doubles as Vitest config
Testing: Vitest 3 with globals:true (no explicit imports for describe/it/expect); jsdom environment; @testing-library/react + @testing-library/jest-dom
CSS: plain CSS files (no modules, no Tailwind, no CSS-in-JS); App.css exists at src/; styles/style.css also exists but is not the target import
SortSelect onChange fix must cast as FilterState['sortBy'] not 'as any'; verbatimModuleSyntax is active so type imports must stay as 'import type'

App.tsx: derives categories memo from products; computes visibleProducts via filterProducts(); renders toolbar + results + pagination
ProductCard.tsx: renders article card using id, name, category, description, price, discountPct (optional), rating, reviewCount, tags, inStock

SortSelect.tsx: onChange prop typed as (sortBy: FilterState['sortBy']) => void; receives e.target.value (string) without a cast — type mismatch

Features that must not regress: category filtering, sort by price/rating, client-side filtering, pagination, results count, discount badge, in-stock status, tag rendering, loading spinner, error alert
